explanation.text: Automation means letting Python do the boring jobs for you. Many of those jobs are about files: reading them, writing them, and sorting them into folders.
On this site your files live in a practice folder. It is empty at the start of every run and cleared at the end, so you can experiment safely. On your own computer, the same code works on real files.
`pathlib` is the tool for this. A `Path` is a file name or a folder name.

explanation.code:
from pathlib import Path

note = Path("note.txt")
note.write_text("Hello\nWorld")   # make the file
print(note.read_text())          # read it back

explanation.text: A few more things a `Path` can do:

explanation.code:
folder = Path("reports")
folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)           # make a folder (no error if it exists)
file = folder / "may.txt"             # "/" joins a folder and a file name
print(file.name, file.stem, file.suffix)   # may.txt may .txt
print(file.exists())                  # False until you write it
files = sorted(folder.glob("*.txt"))  # find all .txt files, in order

explanation.text: `read_text().splitlines()` gives you the lines of a file as a list. To add to the end of a file without erasing it, open it in append mode, with `"a"`.

explanation.code:
with open("log.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write("job finished\n")

explanation.text: Always try a new file script on COPIES of your files first. A script that renames or deletes files cannot be undone.

explanation.title: rename files safely
explanation.text: This script adds a date to the start of every `.txt` file name in a folder. It starts in **dry run** mode: it only shows what it would do. Change `DRY_RUN` to `False` only when the preview looks right.
explanation.code:
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import date

folder = Path("my_files")   # a folder with COPIES of your files
DRY_RUN = True              # True = only show what would happen

for file in sorted(folder.glob("*.txt")):
    new_name = f"{date.today()}_{file.name}"
    print(file.name, "->", new_name)
    if not DRY_RUN:
        file.rename(folder / new_name)

examples.title: Write and read a file
examples.code:
from pathlib import Path

note = Path("note.txt")
note.write_text("Hello\nWorld")
print(note.exists())
print(note.read_text())
print(note.read_text().splitlines())

examples.title: Make a folder and list its files
examples.code:
from pathlib import Path

folder = Path("reports")
folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
for name in ["march.txt", "april.txt", "notes.md"]:
    (folder / name).write_text("data")

for file in sorted(folder.glob("*.txt")):
    print(file.name, file.stem, file.suffix)

examples.title: Add lines to a log file
examples.code:
for message in ["started", "working", "done"]:
    with open("log.txt", "a") as f:
        f.write(message + "\n")

print(open("log.txt").read())

from pathlib import Path

folder = Path("invoices")
folder.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
for name in ["jan.pdf", "feb.pdf", "feb.txt", "mar.pdf", "notes.md"]:
    (folder / name).write_text("x")

quiz.question: Which line writes text into a file?
quiz.explanation: `write_text()` makes the file and puts the text in it.

quiz.question: What does `Path("reports") / "may.txt"` make?
quiz.explanation: For a Path, `/` joins a folder and a file name.

quiz.question: Why should a new file script start with a "dry run"?
options: You see what would change before anything really changes
quiz.explanation: Renaming and deleting cannot be undone, so look at the plan first.
